prompt: Which condition is necessary and sufficient for failure of transitivity of $R$? All variables range over its domain; they need not be distinct.

answers.explanation: One two-step chain without its shortcut suffices. In particular, repeated endpoints can witness failure when a two-way pair lacks a loop.
This demands that every chain lacks a shortcut and can hold vacuously when no chain exists. Failure of transitivity requires at least one chain without its shortcut.
A one-way pair concerns symmetry, not transitivity.
Missing a loop alone does not violate transitivity.
A chain with its shortcut is compatible with transitivity; a missing shortcut is needed.
One of the two edges does not form a two-step chain.
Failure needs one triple, not every triple; the universal condition is also vacuous on an empty domain.

answers.explanation: This misses repeated-endpoint violations: a loopless two-way pair on two elements is not transitive.
The two pairs converge at a common target rather than forming a chain.
The required shortcut runs from the first element to the third, not in reverse.
